message.content:
**Proteins that are typically found in the plasma membrane** | Category | Function | Representative Examples | |----------|----------|------------------------| | **Integral (transmembrane) proteins** | Span the lipid bilayer; often act as channels, transporters, or receptors. | • **Na⁺/K⁺‑ATPase** (ion pump)
• **Glucose transporter 1 (GLUT1)** (facilitated diffusion)
• **Aquaporin‑4** (water channel)
• **G‑protein coupled receptors (GPCRs)** – e.g., β‑adrenergic receptor, muscarinic acetylcholine receptor
• **Ionotropic glutamate receptors** (e.g., NMDA receptor)
• **Voltage‑gated ion channels** – e.g., Na⁺, K⁺, Ca²⁺ channels
• **Connexins** (gap‑junction hemichannels)
• **Integrins** (cell‑matrix adhesion)
• **Cadherins** (cell‑cell adhesion)
• **Receptor tyrosine kinases** – e.g., EGFR, HER2 | | **Peripheral (non‑integral) proteins** | Associate with the membrane surface via lipid anchors or interactions with integral proteins. | • **Ankyrin** (links integral proteins to the cytoskeleton)
• **Spectrin** (provides membrane stability)
• **Band‑3 protein** (anion exchanger in erythrocytes, peripheral to the membrane)
• **Glycophorin A** (erythrocyte membrane protein, peripheral) | | **Lipid‑anchored proteins** | Covalently attached to lipids (e.g., GPI anchors) and reside on the outer leaflet. | • **CD59** (protectin, GPI‑anchored)
• **Prion protein (PrP^C)** (GPI‑anchored)
• **CD55 (decay‑accelerating factor)** (GPI‑anchored) | | **Extracellular matrix‑binding proteins** | Interact with the extracellular matrix or other cells. | • **Fibronectin** (integrin ligand)
• **Collagen type IV** (basement membrane component) | ### Quick Take‑away - **Integral proteins** are the most common and include ion channels, transporters, receptors, and adhesion molecules. - **Peripheral proteins** attach to the membrane surface or to integral proteins and help maintain structure and signaling. - **Lipid‑anchored proteins** are tethered to the outer leaflet via lipid modifications and often participate in signaling or immune functions. These proteins together give the plasma membrane its selective permeability, signaling capabilities, and structural integrity.
